spending — What was spent over a window (default: the last twelve months). view=summary: per period. categories: per period and category, with its share. transactions: the lines with merchant and category. fees: what each portfolio, or account outside one, paid in fees, net of refunds, beside its mean value, annualized fee rate and return; a trust's or a plan's fees count. spend and refunds are positive; net_spend = spend - refunds. Card payments, transfers and mortgage payments are never spending: they are in cashflow. Example: {view: "categories", from: "2025", to: "2025"}.

Parameters (all optional):
  from         Window start; snaps to the unit's start.
  to           Window end; snaps to the unit's end. Default today unless the tool says otherwise.
  view         summary | categories | transactions | fees. Which rows to return (default summary).
  period       daily | weekly | monthly | quarterly | annual | total. Bucket size (default total: one row per category for the whole window).
  level        primary | detailed. Category vocabulary of the categories view: primary (default, broad groups) or detailed.
  source       Keep this source id only (e.g. "schwab"); a comma list keeps several.
  account      Keep rows whose account name, id or nickname contains this (case-insensitive).
  category     Keep categories whose label or id contains this (e.g. "groceries"); implies level=detailed.
  merchant     transactions only: keep only rows whose merchant contains this text.
  currency     Output currency, e.g. USD or CHF. Default: the configured one.
  filter       Conditions, all of which hold: ["value > 1000", "date >= 2025-07", "category not in Rent, Groceries"].
  search       Keep rows with this text in any cell.
  columns      "default", "all", names, or "+add,-remove"; describe(topic=<tool>) lists them.
  sort         Column to sort by; "-" for descending. "-value": the main money column, largest first whatever the sign.
  max_chars    Most characters the result may take (default 16000); the page ends at a row boundary and the last line says how to get the rest.
  limit        Most rows to return (default: as many as fit).
  offset       Rows to skip (default 0).
  format       table | csv | json. Result format (default table).

Columns (* = shown by default; columns=all shows every one):
  summary: period*, period_start, txn_count*, spend_USD*, refunds_USD*, net_spend_USD*
  categories: period*, period_start, category*, category_id, txn_count*, spend_USD*, refunds_USD*, net_spend_USD*, share_pct*
  transactions: silver_source*, date*, datetime, account*, account_id, account_kind, account_nickname, account_category, kind, merchant*, merchant_signature, spend_primary, spend_detailed, category*, category_primary, issuer_category, issuer_category_id, provenance, counterparty, description, currency*, net_amount*, value_USD*, tx_id
  fees: period*, start_date, end_date, silver_source*, entity_kind, entity*, entity_id, fees_USD*, fees_investment_USD, fees_bank_USD, fees_atm_USD, fees_other_USD, mean_value_USD*, fee_rate_pct*, twr_pct*, quality*

Filters each view takes (a filter the view lacks moves the call to the first finer view that has it):
  summary: none
  categories: category
  transactions: source, account, category, merchant
Outside that order (a view of its own, which no filter moves a call to or from):
  fees: source, account

spend and refunds are positive; net_spend = spend - refunds. The category rows of a period sum to its summary row. (uncategorized) is what no rule or model has placed yet. The transactions view keeps the ledger sign: a purchase is negative there. fees is per portfolio, else per account outside one: fees are the primary BANK_FEES lines net of refunds, trading costs and fund costs are not in them, fee_rate_pct is fees over mean_value annualized and blank where the mean value is not above zero, and twr_pct is the entity's monthly returns chained over the months that end in the window, blank where returns has none. Returns stay net of fees.
Example: {view: "transactions", from: "2025-03", to: "2025-03", sort: "-value", limit: 10}.

This endpoint redacts amounts, quantities, account numbers and the names taken off statements (merchants, payers, narratives), and shows a name a person typed about an account as a pseudonym such as manual-1, or as its account number, redacted; source ids, other account names, holdings and their names, categories and shares stay visible.
